payload.selection_rationale: One proposal (practice), taken as the spine because it matches what is in the tree. Option (b), keep the wait and say so, is already built at eafb1c3. The product change is StoppingWait.cs, one TextBlock and about 26 lines in MainWindow.xaml.cs. Scanner, SynchronousIoCancel and the store are untouched. Code review confirmed the placement by reading the tree. The spikes agree: 0 of 15 in-process cancels returned early, so the only faster route is abandoning the thread. That keeps a store alive after Cancel, needs a late-write guard in the counting path, and has no retention design against the U-001 figure of 699 MiB for 5M entries. The UI gap was at most 237 ms across 64-70 s stalls, and the process was gone within 345 ms in 6 of 6 runs. Nothing here needs a new component, and reversing to (a) later is new work, not a rewrite of (b). The proposal's aim matches the reflect lessons: the person decides C2 themselves, and no stage attempts a check that changes SMB mappings. Two of its claims did not survive against the record and were rewritten, with a third declined as unverifiable; see coherence_check. The survey's C3, C4 and C5 states are superseded by the build and code-review accounts (builds#84, reviews#86). C1 stays cut as already measured.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Its spine is kept: (b) as the target, the design document rewritten to the code at eafb1c3, the M2 and m5 overrides, and person-run network checks. Amended: the index.json hand-edit dropped, the staleness rule made consistent with its own comment fix, the fitness rules re-cut, and the cross-domain block hedged. The handed text was clipped at 20,000 characters, so its risk section was not seen.

components.name: Stopping wait line lifecycle
components.responsibility: OnCancel starts a nullable Stopwatch. The existing 250 ms progress DispatcherTimer calls ShowStopping, which reads only that clock and shows StoppingDetail from 2 s after Cancel. EndStopping sits beside _timer.Stop() in StartScan's single finally, which wraps both the scan await and UnlessCancelled, and it runs before ScanningPanel collapses. After that finally _cancel is null, and OnClosing calls _cancel?.Cancel(), not OnCancel. So no clock can outlive its run and no second scan can inherit a stale line. Cancel still waits for the scan; the thread is never abandoned.
components.key_interactions: The detail TextBlock is StoppingDetail in MainWindow.xaml. The wording comes from StoppingWait.For. The hook reads the same window state through the schema-1 report path and its own log. The Scan Engine, SynchronousIoCancel and the store are not touched.

components.name: Stopping wording (pure function)
components.responsibility: StoppingWait.For(elapsed) returns the detail text for an elapsed time since Cancel. It shows nothing before 2 s. From 2 s it shows a count-up in whole seconds and names closing the window as the escape. From 90 s it switches to wording that gives no estimate. It promises no end time, never counts down, and does not claim the drive is a network drive. The criterion is that property list. Exact strings are pinned by StoppingWaitTests at eafb1c3 (-5 s, -1 ms, 0, 1.999 s, 2 s, 89.999 s, 90 s, 3600 s).
components.key_interactions: Compiled into Core.Tests as a linked file, so its boundaries are tested with no window. It takes elapsed as an input and reads no clock.

components.name: Window hook (armed mode)
components.responsibility: Waits for the rig's armed marker, with a fixed 60 s deadline from hook load. An unset FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS means no Cancel; WindowCases.ps1 sets 3000 explicitly for the wait-line case. An armed close checks that ScanningPanel is still visible, because OnCancel disables CancelButton. From Cancel a 250 ms timer writes 'stopping' lines. 'returned ms=' is written when ScanningPanel collapses, which is after EndStopping in the same finally, so an uncleared line would still be caught. One final 'stopping' line comes from Dispatcher.ShutdownStarted.
components.key_interactions: Read by the CheckWaitLine and CheckCloseEscape checks in WindowCases.ps1. Drift accepted: the 250 ms stopping timer stops at scan return, not at window close.

components.name: Window cases
components.responsibility: C-006 runs by default and proves only that no wait line appears on an ordinary local cancel; it cannot tell a working line from a missing one. The -IncludeNetwork cases are run only by a person. N-001: the first non-empty detail appears 1.9-3 s after Cancel, the count never goes down, no gap between consecutive 'stopping' lines exceeds 1 s, the final detail is '-', and Cancel-to-return is reported from the 'returned' stamp. N-002: closing the window during a stall, both after a Cancel and with no Cancel. N-003: a second rig run waits or fails with an error that says why. N-004: a killed run's leftover mapping does not block the next run. A network case named without -IncludeNetwork prints NOT RUN and exits 2.
components.key_interactions: Builds StallRig through Update-StallRig, which mirrors Update-Hook. The check functions were also fed 19 synthetic logs (2 good wait logs pass, 10 wait-line mutants fail, 2 good close logs pass, 5 close mutants fail). WindowMutants.ps1 keeps its 8 mutants.

components.name: Stall rig with per-session isolation
components.responsibility: The SMBLibrary server plus StallingFileStore, extracted unchanged from StalledShareTests. RigLock is a named mutex, Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig, held for the rig's life, and it is scoped to one sign-in session. While holding it the rig sweeps leftover mappings that exactly match the 127.0.0.1 share named fsa plus 8 hex digits. It never touches a mapping to any other server, so the person's Z: is safe. It unmaps on normal exit or stdin close, and after a kill the next run's sweep covers it.
components.key_interactions: Linked by StalledShareTests.cs and StallRig. Covered by SmbRigTests (17 tests). The SmbRig.cs comments that say 'machine-wide' are corrected to 'per sign-in session'.

components.name: StallRig console
components.responsibility: A self-contained win-x64 console, because this machine has no machine-wide .NET 10 runtime and a framework-dependent build exited -2147450730. It builds its tree in a 'tree' folder next to --marker, so a killed run's tree stays inside the case folder that is removed. It writes the marker when the stall is armed, unmaps when stdin closes, and exits 2 with a usage line on bad arguments.
components.key_interactions: Started and stopped by the N cases. Takes RigLock through the linked SmbRig.cs.

components.name: Architecture rules
components.responsibility: Four tripwires in the file SL-022 created, appended under the Q-010 rule. (1) The wording is pure. (2) Nothing abandons the scan wait. (3) and (4) Only SmbRig.cs changes SMB mappings, once for .cs and once for .ps1. Gates run CodeGraph op=rebuild first, because the import rule reports UNRAN on a fresh tree.
components.key_interactions: Checked by taad3.fitness. Fitness passed all 25 rules at build, code review and validate.

components.name: Decision record
components.responsibility: The SL-020 document section records six things. (b) is chosen, pending the person's own acceptance. Abandoning is rejected, with the spike 1, 3 and 4 numbers. 'Closing the window quits at once' rests on the loopback rig until the real-disconnect protocol runs. The rig lock is per session. The conditions that reopen the question. The person-run network check and its staleness rule.
components.key_interactions: No runtime role. It is where the next slice that touches Cancel looks. It is not on the staleness path list.

contracts.name: Stopping state text
contracts.notes: Cancel to 2 s: 'Stopping...' only. From 2 s: StoppingDetail shows StoppingWait.For(elapsed) with whole elapsed seconds and the close escape. From 90 s: wording that gives no estimate. On scan return the detail collapses in the single finally, before ScanningPanel collapses. There is no countdown and no new button.
contracts.error_cases: The scan never returns: the count keeps climbing and closing the window is the escape. That escape is measured on the loopback rig only. A local cancel slower than 2 s (SynchronousIoCancelTests flakes 3 of 50 class runs): the line flashes and its conditional wording stays true. The scan faults or finishes on its own while the line shows: it collapses in the same finally, and no test feeds it.

contracts.name: StoppingWait.For
contracts.notes: Pure. Input is elapsed since Cancel, including negative values. Output is the detail text to show, and nothing to show below 2 s. It reads no clock and imports no WPF or Win32.
contracts.error_cases: Negative elapsed shows nothing. Elapsed of an hour shows the no-estimate wording without overflow.

contracts.name: Closing the window while stopping
contracts.notes: The window is hidden within 1 s and the process is gone within 5 s of Close, with or without a prior Cancel. Measured on the loopback rig: window hidden 29 ms or less, process gone 345 ms or less, 6 of 6 (spike 4). N-002 reportedly passed at validate #4. Unmeasured after a real Wi-Fi drop, tunnel drop or sleep-resume.
contracts.error_cases: If a real disconnect leaves the process alive until the client timeout, the escape does not exist. See the decidable disagreement.

contracts.name: Hook log
contracts.notes: 'stopping ms=<since cancel> title=<text> detail=<text|->' every 250 ms from Cancel to return. 'returned ms=<since cancel>' when ScanningPanel collapses. One final 'stopping' line from ShutdownStarted. FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS unset means no Cancel. The marker deadline is 60 s from hook load.
contracts.error_cases: Marker absent at 60 s: the hook refuses, logs why and presses nothing. Stop with no delay, or an armed throw: refused as an invalid configuration. An armed close after a fast local cancel: refused with 'scan no longer running'.

contracts.name: StallRig launch
contracts.notes: StallRig.exe --marker <path> takes RigLock, sweeps rig-shaped leftovers under it, maps one 127.0.0.1 share named fsa plus 8 hex digits, writes the marker when the stall is armed, and unmaps when stdin closes or on normal exit. It has an optional wait argument the builder added.
contracts.error_cases: Lock held by a live run: it waits or fails with a message naming the lock (N-003). A killed previous run: the next run's sweep removes its mapping (N-004). A leftover from another logon session, such as an elevated one: invisible to the sweep, so New-SmbMapping fails loudly. Bad arguments: exit 2 with a usage line.

contracts.name: The person-run network check
contracts.notes: Run by a person, never attempted by a stage: WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork under pwsh, then the Core.Tests project filtered to Network=SMB-LOOPBACK. The record carries the HEAD it ran at, pass or fail for N-001 to N-004 and StalledShareTests, and N-001's measured Cancel-to-return. A stage that finds no record, or a stale one, reports 'owed to a person' once and does not retry. The pass goes stale only if a later commit changes executable lines in the app files MainWindow.xaml, MainWindow.xaml.cs or StoppingWait.cs, in tests/window/FsaWindowHook/ or tests/window/StallRig/, in SmbRig.cs or StalledShareTests.cs, or in the N cases and checks of WindowCases.ps1. A comment-only diff does not make it stale.
contracts.error_cases: The permission classifier refused this as [Modify Shared Resources] in build-check, build and validate. A named network case run without -IncludeNetwork exits 2 (NOT RUN), which is not a pass.

key_decisions.decision: Option (b) is this design's target. C2 closes only when the person accepts it themselves at the design halt, recorded as theirs. The model-contact discharge of O-002 does not count. Option (a), abandoning the scan thread, is not built. If the person chooses (a), eafb1c3 is not merged and a new design pass is needed. It would have to measure retention of an abandoned store against the 1 GB budget (U-001 peaked at 699 MiB), guard late writes in the Scan Engine at counting-rule risk, and delete architecture rule 2.
key_decisions.rationale: The slice exists to put this choice before a person. Reflect found a model made it in the owner's absence and disposed of all 10 review findings. The evidence for (b) is strong: 0 of 15 in-process cancels returned early, the UI gap was 237 ms at most, and the process was gone in 345 ms or less. The (b) code is small and stays useful next to (a).

key_decisions.decision: The design document targets the code at eafb1c3. The accepted findings (M1, m1, m2, m3, m4, m6, m7) and the builder's declared deviations are folded into it: the O-002 wording, the self-contained StallRig, the ScanningPanel check for an armed close, the 'returned' stamp from the ScanningPanel collapse, SMBLibrary.Win32 1.5.8 to match Core.Tests, and the N-001 to N-004 names. The criterion is the property list on the wording, not the strings, which StoppingWaitTests pin.
key_decisions.rationale: Every gate reads this document. If it still described the pre-build shape, each stage would judge correct code against a target it had rightly left. The design must own the criterion, and a criterion of 'whatever the code returns' owns nothing, so the properties are written down.

key_decisions.decision: M2 and m5 stay overridden. EndStopping stays beside _timer.Stop() in the single finally, and the N-001 upper bound stays 3 s.
key_decisions.rationale: Both rest on lines anyone can read. The timer is fixed at 250 ms, the finally wraps the scan await and UnlessCancelled, and code review confirmed the placement.

key_decisions.decision: Every check that changes SMB mappings (N-001 to N-004, and StalledShareTests on the extracted rig) is a named step a person runs. Stages read the recorded result and never retry the command. The result goes stale only by the path list in the contract. StalledShareTests joins that sitting because it was rewritten (+2 -311) and has never run since.
key_decisions.rationale: The classifier refused the operation in build-check, build and validate. Validate looped three times at one HEAD with the same refusal, and only a person's run ended it. One 70 s command is cheaper than another loop.

key_decisions.decision: RigLock keeps its Local\ name. The comments in SmbRig.cs that say 'machine-wide' are corrected to 'per sign-in session'. The decision record states that runs from different sign-in sessions are not serialised. A comment-only edit to SmbRig.cs does not stale the person's pass. The reviewer confirms from git diff that the file has no changed code lines.
key_decisions.rationale: Nothing in this repo runs the rig from two sessions, and the person is one. Renaming to Global\ changes behaviour on a file the person's pass already covers, to fix what is a wording drift. The proposal's own stale list named SmbRig.cs, so a comment fix would have voided the pass it relied on. The stale rule is redefined to cover behaviour.

key_decisions.decision: If the commit failed on a trunk conflict, the engine's conflict route decides who rebases slice/SL-038 onto uat. The design fixes only what follows. The four fitness rules are appended after whatever .taad/fitness.yaml holds on trunk (a union, since the file is append-only under Q-010). Then the default suite, the default window run, WindowMutants and fitness after a CodeGraph rebuild are re-run. The person's pass is reused unless a listed path changed in executable lines.
key_decisions.rationale: The branch touches four files other slices also edit: fitness.yaml, SL-020-scanner.md, WindowCases.ps1 and StartupHook.cs. The commit record gives no reason for the failure, so this is conditional and does nothing if the cause was something else.

key_decisions.decision: The O-008 split is made through the engine's obligation disposition, not a hand-edit of .taad/slices/SL-038/index.json. The cancelled-cleanly shape is covered by N-001. The faulted and finished-on-its-own shapes are recorded as not fed by any test. They are minor and not worth a lap.
key_decisions.rationale: index.json is the engine's derived record, and a hand-edit would be overwritten or contradicted by the next derive. The proposal named it as a build target. Nothing can feed those shapes: the shipped exe has no seam and the SL-033 rule at .taad/fitness.yaml forbids adding one.

key_decisions.decision: The real-disconnect protocol (Wi-Fi off, tailscale down, sleep about 2 minutes, 3 runs each, one timed Close per mode) is carried to SC-033 as a person-run item. This slice's merge does not wait for it. The UI wording stays conditional, and the 'closing quits at once' clause is recorded as resting on rig evidence.
key_decisions.rationale: No stage may cut the network. The spike ran 0 of 9. Reflect already carried it to SC-033. The wording promises no end, so an unbounded wait does not make the text false. Only a failing Close would, and that is the decidable disagreement.

key_decisions.decision: Four fitness rules stand: (1) wording is pure, (2) no abandon, (3) mappings only in SmbRig.cs for .cs files, (4) the same for .ps1 files. Before rule 4 is declared, build greps tests/**/*.ps1 for the patterns. If WindowCases.ps1 changes a mapping directly, route it through StallRig; do not add an except.
key_decisions.rationale: Critique m1 said the mapping rule missed .ps1 and 'net use'. No account shows whether the widening was built. A rule that fires on correct code gets deleted, and one that matches nothing never fails.

key_decisions.decision: The SynchronousIoCancelTests flake (3 of 50 repeated class runs, 1 of 2 full-suite runs) is its own slice and is not fixed here.
key_decisions.rationale: It predates SL-038, and this slice does not touch Scanner or SynchronousIoCancel. It sits on the 2 s bound the wait line uses. If a local cancel really crosses 2 s the line flashes, and its wording stays true.

cases.behaviour: show the wait line after Cancel
cases.shape: elapsed since Cancel is under the 2 s gate, including a negative elapsed
cases.why: StoppingWait.For must return nothing, and a negative elapsed must never show a negative count. Pinned by StoppingWaitTests at -5 s, -1 ms, 0 and 1.999 s.

cases.behaviour: show the wait line after Cancel
cases.shape: elapsed is at exactly 2 s and between 2 s and 90 s
cases.why: The gate is inclusive at 2 s. The count is whole seconds, never goes down, and always names closing the window.

cases.behaviour: show the wait line after Cancel
cases.shape: elapsed is at 90 s, or an hour
cases.why: The wording must switch to no estimate and stay stable. Pinned at 89.999 s, 90 s and 3600 s.

cases.behaviour: clear the wait line when the scan returns
cases.shape: Cancel is pressed while the scan is stalled and the scan returns on the SMB client timeout (N-001)
cases.why: This is the only positive proof that the line appears 1.9-3 s after Cancel, counts up, keeps the UI live, and clears in the single finally before ScanningPanel collapses. The 'returned' stamp with detail '-' catches an uncleared line. It needs a person's run.

cases.behaviour: clear the wait line when the scan returns
cases.shape: an ordinary local cancel that returns in milliseconds (C-006)
cases.why: The line must never appear. This is the default run's only guard, and it cannot tell a working line from a missing one.

cases.behaviour: clear the wait line when the scan returns
cases.shape: the scan faults, or finishes on its own, while the line is showing
cases.why: No test can feed it: the shipped exe has no seam and the SL-033 rule forbids adding one. Both paths go through the single finally at MainWindow.xaml.cs:161-177. Left on the matrix so a later slice with an App-level harness can disagree.

cases.behaviour: close the window while a scan is blocked
cases.shape: Cancel was pressed first and the scan thread is blocked in an SMB call (N-002)
cases.why: The escape that makes waiting acceptable: window hidden within 1 s, process gone within 5 s. It reportedly passed at validate #4 on the loopback rig only.

cases.behaviour: close the window while a scan is blocked
cases.shape: no Cancel was pressed, so CancelButton is still enabled, or the scan has already ended locally
cases.why: An armed close must check ScanningPanel, not CancelButton. After a fast local cancel it must be refused with 'scan no longer running' rather than silently pass.

cases.behaviour: close the window after a real disconnect
cases.shape: Wi-Fi off, tunnel down, or sleep and resume mid-scan
cases.why: Not runnable by any stage: it changes the person's network state and the classifier refuses it. It is carried to SC-033 as a person-run protocol and is the empirical question in the decidable disagreement. The reason is recorded so it can be disputed.

cases.shape: the machine also holds the person's own mapping (Z: to 100.109.48.75) and other shares on 127.0.0.1 whose names are not fsa plus exactly 8 hex digits (7 or 9 digits, uppercase, a different name)
cases.why: The sweep deletes mappings. It must remove only rig-shaped ones and never the person's own. SmbRigTests are expected to cover the filter boundary.

cases.shape: a second run starts while the first holds RigLock, or a killed run left a mapping behind (N-003, N-004)
cases.why: The SMB client allows one TCP port per server name, so two rigs on 127.0.0.1 collide. A killed sole holder leaves no abandoned-mutex signal, because Windows destroys the mutex with its last handle. Only the sweep recovers it.

cases.behaviour: run the stalled-share baseline on the extracted rig
cases.shape: StalledShareTests (Network=SMB-LOOPBACK) after the rig moved into Rig/SmbRig.cs
cases.why: The test lost 311 lines and gained 2. It compiles but has never run since the extraction. It needs the person's consent to change mappings, and it takes about 70 s.

cases.shape: code that waits on the scan task with WaitAsync or Task.WhenAny, against UnlessCancelled's running.WaitAsync(token) on the volume query
cases.why: The rule must fire on _scanTask.WaitAsync, Task.WhenAny and the Task.Run chain, and must not fire on the volume-query wait, which is allowed. Code review ran the regexes against samples.

cases.behaviour: start the window hook in armed mode
cases.shape: the marker never appears, stop mode has no delay, or the hook is armed with throw
cases.why: An armed hook that waits forever would hang a case. The hook must refuse and log why after 60 s. Rehearsed by the builder against a local tree.

architecture_rules.name: the stopping wording is a pure function of elapsed time
architecture_rules.because: The file is compiled into Core.Tests as a linked source, and Core.Tests does not reference WPF. Reading a clock or a window inside it would make the 2 s and 90 s boundaries untestable, and the wording tests would need a window. The engine's Fitness import rule reports UNRAN until CodeGraph op=rebuild has run.

architecture_rules.name: Cancel never abandons the scan thread
architecture_rules.because: Abandoning the wait frees the window but leaves the scan thread and its store alive, with late writes into memory that has a 1 GB budget and into counting state. That is option (a), and it needs the person's decision, a retention measurement and a late-write guard first. The volume-query wait, running.WaitAsync(token), is allowed and must not match. A name-based match is a tripwire, not a proof, and review still applies.

architecture_rules.name: only the shared rig changes SMB client mappings (C#)
architecture_rules.because: The Windows SMB client allows one TCP port per server name, so every rig on 127.0.0.1 shares one slot. A second place that maps or removes shares bypasses RigLock and the strict sweep filter, and can delete another run's mapping or the person's own.

architecture_rules.name: only the shared rig changes SMB client mappings (PowerShell)
architecture_rules.because: The same rule for scripts. A window case that maps a share directly skips RigLock and the sweep filter. Mapping goes through StallRig or the rig, which the case starts.

stack_chosen.choice: An in-process SMBLibrary server (1.5.8.1 for the server, SMBLibrary.Win32 1.5.8) mapped through the real Windows SMB client with a non-persistent New-SmbMapping -TcpPort on 127.0.0.1. It is opt-in through Trait Network=SMB-LOOPBACK, which the default VSTestTestCaseFilter excludes, and no engine stage runs it.
stack_chosen.why: The project's stack block does not name it. SL-024 chose it and SL-038 extracted it into Rig/SmbRig.cs. It is the only rig measured to reproduce the ~60 s stall through the real redirector. Recorded so the next slice does not design a second stalled-share rig.

stack_chosen.choice: StallRig is a self-contained win-x64 net10.0-windows console at tests/window/StallRig. WindowCases.ps1's Update-StallRig builds it through eng/dotnet.ps1 into gitignored artifacts/stall-rig. It is outside FsAnalyser.slnx.
stack_chosen.why: Not in the stack block. This machine has no machine-wide .NET 10 runtime, and a framework-dependent build could not start (exit -2147450730). Anything launched outside eng/dotnet.ps1 must be self-contained. It is built like the hook, which is also not in the slnx.

prior_art.pattern: The CIFS/SMB1-era timeout page covers the old exchange timers and points to a separate SMB 2.x/3.0 page. The ~60 s here rests on this machine's measured SessionTimeout of 60 and on the rig (57-66 s), not on this page. That is why the wording promises no end time.

Detection of a lost connection has varied between clients and versions (a 30 s scan period with an echo probe; 32 s and 48 s observed on the wire). This supports counting up rather than promising a figure.

In-flight SMB I/O can be cancelled by the caller only when the application owns the SMB client (go-smb2 context rebinding). It is not available through the Windows redirector, which spike 1 measured: CancelSynchronousIo waited 57-66 s with err 121.

A failure of similar shape at a different layer: a user-mode SMB client whose exit waits on a disconnect response. This is the failure the 'closing the window quits at once' clause must not have after a real disconnect (the decidable disagreement). It is not a kernel-level analogue.
Local\ kernel object names are scoped to the terminal-services session and Global\ spans sessions. Not verified across an elevation boundary; nothing in this repo runs the rig elevated.

Drive mappings belong to a logon session, and an elevated token and an unelevated token have different logon sessions (the EnableLinkedConnections behaviour). This is why a sweep cannot see another session's leftover mapping.
prior_art.where: Windows UAC and network drive mappings

prior_art.pattern: Abandon the wait, not the work (Task.WaitAsync). The costs are an orphaned operation that keeps its state alive and late writes into shared state. That is option (a), which is not recommended.
prior_art.where: .NET Task.WaitAsync; Stephen Toub, 'How do I cancel non-cancelable async operations?'

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Web browsers waiting on an unresponsive host
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: When a network wait cannot be interrupted, keep the window responsive, say what it is waiting on, count up rather than invent an estimate, and keep an escape (closing) that does not depend on the wait ending.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: It transfers partway: the visible status and the live UI. It stops at the browser's stop button, which drops the socket. That is option (a), and spike 1 showed this app cannot do it, because a thread blocked in the redirector is not interruptible. So the analogy supports the wording of (b), not a claim that the wait is avoidable.

invariants.precondition: The UI thread stays responsive throughout the wait
invariants.evidence: Spike 3 measured a maximum tick gap of 237 ms over 64-70 s SMB stalls in 3 runs, with IsHungAppWindow never true. N-001's 1 s gap check reportedly passed at validate #4, but that account is not in the record handed to this design.

invariants.precondition: An escape exists that does not depend on the wait ending
invariants.evidence: Holds on the loopback rig: window hidden 29 ms or less and process gone 345 ms or less in 6 of 6 (spike 4), with N-002 reportedly passing at validate #4. Unmeasured after a real Wi-Fi, tunnel or sleep disconnect.

invariants.precondition: The wait ends on its own within about a minute
invariants.evidence: Only the rig has shown it (57-66 s; validate measured 59.9 s). The real-disconnect experiment ran 0 of 9. The wording gives no end time and switches at 90 s, so it stays true if this fails.

decidable_disagreements.question: After a real disconnect (Wi-Fi off, tunnel drop, sleep-resume), does closing the window still end the process within 5 s, as it did on the loopback rig?
decidable_disagreements.positions: The proposal treats the escape as holding: the rig measured window gone within 29 ms and process gone within 345 ms in 6 of 6, and it ships the 'closing the window quits at once' clause on that evidence. The opposing reading is that a real dead link leaves the redirector in a different state from a silent loopback server, so thread rundown could wait on the client timeout, and closing would only hide the window. Only a person's timed Close per mode can settle it.

taste_disagreements: Whether RigLock should be Local\ (kept) or Global\. Global\ would serialise concurrent runs across sign-in sessions, but the sweep still could not see another session's leftover, and it changes behaviour on a file the person's pass covers.

Whether the scaffolding is proportionate. The product change is about three small files, while the rig, hook, StallRig, four network cases, 29 tests and rules make up most of a +2242 -355 diff. Reflect's lesson is to size by the rig and by who can run it, not by the UI change.
Where the wording lives: in the App project, linked into Core.Tests as a source file, against a home in Core.
Whether the abandon rule is a name-based tripwire (scan\w*.WaitAsync) rather than something structural. It can miss a task named otherwise, and review remains the backstop.
Naming the network window cases N-001 to N-004, and the choice to end the hook's 250 ms stopping timer at scan return rather than at window close.
open_questions: Does the person accept option (b), including that 'closing the window quits at once' rests on the loopback rig until SC-033 measures real disconnects? This is C2. Every review finding on this slice was model-disposed, and the record shows no acceptance by the person. If the person chooses (a), the design needs a new pass with a retention measurement and a late-write guard in the Scan Engine.

Does the merge wait for StalledShareTests (Network=SMB-LOOPBACK) to be run by the person on the extracted rig, or is the slice accepted with it compiled but never exercised? Recommendation: run it. It is one command of about 70 s, and the rewrite removed 311 lines.

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, so there is no composition to check. Nothing in this design has survived a disagreement with another designer, and that is the first thing a reviewer should argue with. The handed proposal was clipped at 20,000 characters after its cross-domain block, so its risk section and any taste notes or channelled experts it named were not seen. I named no experts.

Seams inside the one proposal that I checked and changed:
1. Its staleness path list named SmbRig.cs while its own decision edits comments in SmbRig.cs. That would void the person's pass to fix a comment. Redesigned: staleness is about executable lines, and a comment-only diff does not stale it.
2. It listed .taad/slices/SL-038/index.json as a place to write the O-008 split. That file is the engine's derived record. Redesigned: the split goes through obligation disposition and, being minor, does not cost a lap.
3. It said the Local\ mutex covers elevated and unelevated processes, and also that an elevated run is another logon session. These agree only if namespace scope and logon-session scope are kept apart. I scoped the claim to same-session unelevated runs, which is all this repo does. I flagged the cross-elevation behaviour as unverified. It also dismissed Global\ as not fixing the cross-session gap. That is true only of leftovers; concurrent runs would be serialised. Kept Local\ as a taste call.
4. Its rule 3 was in a .cs-only form, and I could not confirm the .ps1 widening was ever built. I split it in two and added a build-time grep that routes any direct mapping through StallRig instead of an except. The .ps1 half is unverified against the tree.
5. Its conditional rebase named a builder as the actor. commit-slice has no model, so the engine's conflict route decides. The design only fixes what is re-run afterwards.

What is not established. The N-001 to N-004 pass at validate #4 comes only from the reflection's account. The validate record I was handed is attempt 3, and it ended with those cases not run. No measured N-001 Cancel-to-return figure is in the record, so the person's run contract requires one. The survey I was given predates the build, and its C3, C4 and C5 states are superseded by the build and code-review accounts.

Stages that should have recorded something: commit-slice failed and recorded no reason, so the design cannot tell a trunk conflict from a gate refusal. design-slice (designs#23) and critique-review (reviews#85) each recorded no account. None of this blocks the design.

Rules 1 to 4 are new declarations of the built forms. No rule was invented to fill the field.
